reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 2)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Read the section whole first ('Your inherited parent script': 'One important thing to become aware of ... is your inherited parent script. Your parent script is made up of a collection of rules ... It doesn’t always take the form of a voice. This is not the inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) that you consciously build. Often this script acts as a critic or warden ...'). The draft sits in CONTEXT.txt once, character for character (curly apostrophes match), between the unchanged opener and the unchanged critic/warden sentence. It does what the_change says: three sentences in place of the source's two (what the script is, that it is not always a voice, that it is not the inner adult), in the source's order, with 'This' (not Emulate's 'It') opening the third. Meaning against SOURCE: 'the set of rules and ways of treating yourself that you internalized as a child, mostly based on how your parent(s) treated you' = 'a collection of rules and ways of treating yourself that you adopted as a child (mostly based on how you were treated by your parent(s))' (internalized/adopted is a slight shade, but the parenthetical still carries the parental origin and 'mostly' is kept); 'doesn’t always sound like a voice' = 'doesn’t always take the form of a voice'; 'not the same as your inner adult ... that you build up on purpose' = 'not the inner adult ... that you consciously build'. Nothing is dropped and nothing added: no new claim, no first-person fact, no study or named thing beyond the guide's own Nurturer, Protector, Guide. Seam check: it reads as a plain definition between a plain opener and the livelier critic/warden/'fake' sentences; I felt no different writer and no hedge he would not write ('mostly' and 'doesn’t always' are already in the source). The nearest thing to a seam is the echo 'your inherited parent script. Your parent script', the term restated as the subject where the source said 'This'; it is the term being defined right after it is named, and 'this script' and 'the script' follow, so the repetition does a job (T26 not tripped). The third sentence's 'This' comes straight after 'a voice', so for a beat it could point at the voice, but the whole paragraph is about the script, the source had the same 'This' after 'voice', and the next sentence says 'this script', so the referent holds (C02 not tripped; the weakest spot, and not one I would stop it for). Rows: I found no row actually happening. T02 and T12: the two short negations are distinctions that keep the inherited script apart from the inner adult the guide teaches the reader to build, and they lead into concrete material (critic or warden, 'not to cry', 'fake'); they are not a run of compressed commands or a tidy A/B pair. T06: 'rules and ways of treating yourself' is abstract, but it is the definition of the article's own term and the next, unchanged sentence supplies the specifics. T16: not tripped, there is no 'not X, it's Y' and the positive comes in the next sentence. T17 and T21: one definition with a relative clause and a parenthetical, not a principle and not several argumentative jobs. T15: the wording differs from the source in Emulate's own turns ('made up of a collection of', 'take the form of', 'consciously build') and the sentence shapes are reshaped too, not a swap that leaves another tell standing. T01, T03 to T05, T07, T08, T10, T11, T14, T18 to T20, T22 to T25, T27 to T29, C01, C03 and C04 are absent (no first person, no scene, no filler, no colon, no tic word, no closer; the draft is mid-paragraph; the inner child is not named in it). Linter findings: 'D9 follows the source order' is accepted, because the order is the natural one for a definition (say what it is, then what it is not) and each part notices something: the 'mostly' aside on where the rules come from, the counterexample that it is not always heard as a voice, and the callback to the inner adult the reader builds; so T13 and T09 are absent, since the three sentences carry different weight (32, 9 and 13 words) and the paragraph's weight lands on the unchanged critic/warden list and the 'fake' line. 'E36/E41 heavy second person' is accepted, because the guide speaks to 'you' throughout and these are the reader's own history and the inner adult the reader builds ('you adopted as a child', 'how you were treated', 'you consciously build'), a definition and not coaching or reassurance; by my count the source it replaces carries the same six second-person words (yourself, you, your, you, your, you) in 51 words against the draft's six in 54, so the density is not new.
